RFC7911-2-1.note: Sentence obliges the ADVERTISING speaker to assign Path Identifiers so that (Prefix, Path Identifier) uniquely identifies a path advertised to a neighbor; forbidden behaviour: ze advertising two different paths for one prefix to one neighbor under the same identifier. The only tagged unit, rib/storage TestPeerRIB_AddPath, inserts two RECEIVED NLRI with distinct ids into the Adj-RIB-In and asserts Len()==2: it proves receive-side keying, a neighbouring rule, and never looks at an identifier ze assigns. The assignment producer is the reactor forward path-id generator (forward_path_id.go); units that do prove this sentence (TestForwardPathIDReleaseReturnsValues, the churn and growth-probe tests, TestForwardPathIDsDifferForCollidingSources) are tagged RFC7911-2-2 instead, quoting this sentence in their prose.

RFC7911-2-2.note: Sentence: a speaker that re-advertises a route MUST generate its own Path Identifier for it. Forbidden behaviour: relaying the received identifier. Negative TestForwardPathIDStableAcrossUpdates: require.NotEqual(uint32(receivedPathID=0xDEADBEEF), first) goes red if the received id is copied; positive TestForwardPathIDsDifferForCollidingSources: two sources both using id 1 must leave with different ids (require.NotEqual(first, second)), red under a relaying implementation. The .ci adj-rib-in-replay-addpath-source asserts ze's 0 against the source's 1 on a running daemon. Several other units tagged here quote and prove RFC7911-2-1's sentence instead (see findings).

RFC7911-3-1.note: Sentence: NLRI encoding MUST be extended by prepending the four-octet Path Identifier field. Forbidden: no field, a field of other size, or the field placed after the prefix. TestWriteNLRI_WithStoredPathID asserts buf[0..3]==0000002a and n==4+Len() (red if absent, mis-sized, or appended, since buf[0] would then be the prefix length); TestWriteNLRI_AddPath disabled subtest asserts n==Len() without ADD-PATH; TestINETWithAddPath decodes 00000001 then 8,10 as id 1 and 10.0.0.0/8; test/plugin/adj-rib-in-replay-addpath-source.ci asserts exact wire hex 00000000180A0000 vs 180A0000 per destination negotiation.

RFC7911-4-1.note: Sentence obliges a speaker that WISHES TO INDICATE support for several AFI/SAFIs (the sender of OPEN) to put them in a single ADD-PATH capability instance; forbidden behaviour: ze emitting one code-69 capability per family. Both tagged units (TestAddPathCapability, TestAddPathMultipleFamilies in internal/core/bgp/capability/capability_test.go) drive Parse over hand-built bytes and assert len(caps)==1: they prove the DECODER accepts one instance, a neighbouring rule. No tagged unit encodes ze's own capability set for two ADD-PATH families and counts code-69 instances in the OPEN ze sends.

RFC7911-5-1.note: Quoted sentence: to send multiple paths the speaker MUST advertise Send/Receive 2 or 3 and MUST receive 1 or 3 from the peer, for the corresponding <AFI, SAFI>. Clause 'local advertises 2 or 3': TestFromNegotiatedAddPath rows Receive/Send and Receive/Both require wantSend false (red if a Receive-only local could send). Clause 'peer sent 1 or 3': rows Send/Send and Both/Send require wantSend false. Clause 'for the corresponding <AFI, SAFI>': no tagged unit negotiates ADD-PATH for one family on one side and another family on the other; baseCapsWithAddPath uses one family on both sides and only ipv4Family is read, so a family-blind Negotiate stays green.

RFC7911-5-2.note: Same sentence as RFC7911-5-1 (the row's obligation is the second MUST: receive Send/Receive 1 or 3 from the peer). TestFromNegotiatedAddPath rows Send/Send and Both/Send require wantSend false, red if ze sends when the peer never advertised Receive; TestNegotiateAddPath asserts AddPathSend for Both/Receive. The per-<AFI, SAFI> clause has no assertion: every tagged case puts the same single family on both sides, so a Negotiate that paired the peer's Receive for IPv6 with local Send for IPv4 would pass.

RFC7911-5-3.note: Quoted span: MUST follow RFC 4271 procedures for an <AFI, SAFI> unless ADD-PATH send is advertised and receive is received for it. Forbidden: emitting Path Identifiers to a peer that did not negotiate. TestForwardSplitConvertsAddPathContext (negative) asserts every destination prefix is 4 bytes and equals the plain NLRI; TestForwardPathIDLeavesNonAddPathDestinationAlone likewise. Positive TestForwardSplitSameContextKeepsRawSplit asserts the extended encoding. Per-<AFI, SAFI> clause unasserted: fixtures set ADD-PATH for IPv4 unicast only and send only IPv4, so a family-blind generator passes. TestRFC7606Section54ReadsTypedNLRIUnderAddPath is tagged 5-3 positive but proves receive-side parsing (RFC7911-5-5's rule).

RFC7911-5-4.note: Quoted sentence: follow RFC 4271 unless ADD-PATH negotiated for the <AFI, SAFI>, in which case MUST generate updates based on the combination of prefix and Path Identifier with the extended NLRI encoding. Plain encoding when not negotiated: TestWriteAnnounceUpdateWithAddPath nNoAddPath+4==nAddPath and TestSplitUpdateEndToEnd. Extended encoding when negotiated: TestSplitUpdateAddPathEndToEnd round-trips 4-octet ids. Unasserted: 'based on the combination of the address prefix and the Path Identifier' (no 5-4 unit sends two paths for one prefix and asserts both are generated, so a prefix-keyed generator passes), and the per-<AFI, SAFI> clause. TestForwardPathIDWithdrawOfUnknownPathLeavesNothing is tagged 5-4 but quotes and proves RFC7911-5-6.

RFC7911-5-5.note: Forbidden: applying one <AFI, SAFI>'s ADD-PATH state to another. TestRFC7911AddPathStateAppliesPerFamily negotiates ADD-PATH for exactly one of IPv4/IPv6 unicast and asserts the exact RFC 7606 action per family: path-id encoding accepted only for the ADD-PATH family, plain encoding accepted only for the other, each wrong pairing SessionReset, on both orientations. Buffers are chosen so the misread is structurally fatal (path-id octet 0x21/0x81 as prefix length), isolating the per-family parse choice.
